cards.question: What is main in a Java program?
expected_answer: the place where the program starts
its lines run from top to bottom, in order

cards.question: What does System.out.println("...") do?
expected_answer: prints the text between the quotes to the console
one println = one line

cards.question: What does ; do in Java, and what is a // line?
expected_answer: every instruction ends with ; like a full stop
// starts a comment: a note for humans that Java skips

cards.question: A compile error appears. What do you look at first?
expected_answer: the file name and line number
the message: what Java expected
fix the first error first, then run again

cards.question: What does int balance = 100; mean, part by part?
expected_answer: int = type: whole numbers
balance = the name of the box
100 = the starting value

cards.question: What does balance = balance - 30; do?
expected_answer: takes the CURRENT value of balance
subtracts 30
stores the result back in balance (the old value is gone)

cards.question: What is 7 / 2 in Java, and why?
expected_answer: int divided by int drops the decimals (no rounding, just cut off)

cards.question: What does % give you? What is 10 % 3?
expected_answer: the leftover (remainder) of a division

cards.question: When do you use int, double and boolean?
expected_answer: int: whole numbers (count, cents)
double: numbers with decimals (4.50)
boolean: only true or false (yes/no)

cards.question: What does possible lossy conversion from double to int mean?
expected_answer: you are putting a decimal into a whole-number box
Java will not throw the decimals away silently: use double (or change the calculation)

cards.question: In Java, what does = do? After cups = plates; which box changed?
expected_answer: = is not equals: it puts the value on the right INTO the box on the left
only cups changed; plates keeps its value

cards.question: What is the difference between = and == ?
expected_answer: = puts a value into a variable
== asks whether two values are equal (gives true or false)

cards.question: What do the operators AND (&&), OR (||) and NOT (!) mean?
expected_answer: && = AND: all must be true
|| = OR: at least one must be true
! = NOT: flips true and false

cards.question: cardBlocked is true when the card is blocked. How do you write the card is NOT blocked, and why not cardBlocked = false?
expected_answer: put ! in front: !cardBlocked flips true and false
a single = puts false INTO the box, it does not ask a question

cards.question: A method computes boolean ok = a >= b; and then does return true; What is wrong?
expected_answer: it always hands back true, whatever the values are
return the box with the real answer: return ok;
